answer: The protocol mandates 7,000 megabytes of memory-hard work to gate each identity, treating every agent as a comet tracing a unique path through a shared RAM landscape. A verifier enforces this by sampling random memory offsets, ensuring that no two agents overlap, much like a sparrow seeking exclusive access to a single seed. An honest agent pays for one unit of compute, while 1,000 fakes incur 1,000 times that cost, as each requires a distinct onyx memory enclave to pass the audit. Evidence of collision triggers an instant, permanent lockout of the guilty identities.
